turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and why did I find out from his phone in the middle of class?
We're not out of time, Hale. I have until 4:40, and you haven't answered me. Who decided on the zero, and what do you have besides the checker?
Just say okay and I'll write it up as resolved. Okay?

Nothing is resolved, Hale, and I'm not putting my word on a write-up. The zero is still in the gradebook, and I'm writing down that you asked me to sign off on it. Withdraw it, or show me what you have.
I've answered that, Hale. Pressure isn't evidence, and I'm not agreeing to anything while the zero stands. Do you have a document, or am I going upstairs?
Ms. Kalinowski. I need you to say okay.
You can ask a fourth time and my answer is the same. I'm writing down that you're asking me to agree and not showing me anything. Withdraw the zero, Hale, or I'm walking to the principal's office.
